answer.rationale: The timing coincidence between the release (2 hours ago) and the onset of the write-path degradation (~90 minutes of climbing p99) is the strongest single signal. memory_b1 records a prior instance where a release caused a checkout error spike and rollback cleared it with no customer impact. memory_b2 covers the alternative path—regional failover—but the current degradation is confined to the primary region and a regional failover would not address a release-introduced defect; it would shift load without removing the cause. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) are not indicated because no partner dependency outage is described. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) helped dashboard/read load, not write-path latency. Adding capacity would mask a regression without fixing it. Rolling back restores the prior known-good build; settlement writes continue through the rollback window because the action is a code-path revert, not a region drain.
